# Results — Study 755 (JOLTS-Quits)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The labour-nowcasting
folklore — **a falling JOLTS quits rate signals fading worker confidence and precedes
equity / cyclical weakness** — tested on the monthly **quits rate** tape (a hardcoded
snapshot of FRED `JTSQUR`, Total Nonfarm, SA, percent) against month-end **SPY**
(yfinance, total-return adjusted) and a **cyclical-minus-defensive** long-short index
(XLY − XLP). We split forward 1/3/6/12-month returns into months when quits momentum is
**falling** vs **rising**, compare each to the unconditional base rate, and add a Welch
*t*, a placebo null, a lead/lag scan and a tradable timing overlay — all under the honest
**2-month JOLTS release lag** (the print for reference month t is only public in month
t+2). Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Quits tape | FRED `JTSQUR` — JOLTS quits rate, Total Nonfarm, SA (percent); **hardcoded monthly snapshot**, as-of 2026-07-13 |
| Equity tape | yfinance daily **SPY** adjusted close (total-return adjusted), month-end sampled |
| Cyclicals tape | **XLY − XLP** (consumer-discretionary minus consumer-staples), monthly-rebalanced long-short, total-return legs |
| Window | 2000-12-31 → 2026-05-31 (**306** months; **25.4** years) |
| Signal | quits momentum = rate vs **3 months** prior (pp); **FALLING** when < 0 |
| Entry / costs | **2-month execution lag** (the JOLTS publication delay — act two month-ends after the reference month); 10 bps one-way per switch on the overlay |

> **Release-lag caveat (the distinguishing detail).** JOLTS is published with a ~5–6-week
> delay: the reference-month-t quits rate is not public until the first week of month
> **t+2**. So the earliest an honest trader acts on the month-t print is the close of
> month t+2 — a **2-month execution lag**, applied once, no look-ahead. This is *more*
> conservative than the 1-month lag of the weekly-claims study (385) and it matters: any
> whisper of a lead is already ~6 weeks stale before you can touch it. The quits series is
> the settled print, not the real-time vintage; JOLTS is revised, and that caveat is named
> on the Signal axis. The 2009 trough (**1.2%**, Aug-2009) and the 2021 "Great Resignation"
> peak (**3.0%**, Nov-2021) are included faithfully.

## The signal — forward SPY returns when quits are FALLING vs the base rate

2-month execution lag; the base column is *all* months. The believers say FALLING quits
should depress the forward return; Welch *t* compares the FALLING-set mean to the
unconditional mean (a real confidence gauge ⇒ **significantly negative** *t*). The placebo
*p* is the share of 20,000 random same-size month draws whose mean forward return is **at
most** the FALLING set's (i.e. as bearish or more).

| horizon | n falling | falling mean | rising mean | base mean | falling down-rate | base down-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 89 | **+0.62%** | +0.94% | +0.84% | 35% | 35% | **−0.40** | 0.308 |
| 3-month  | 88 | **+2.10%** | +2.67% | +2.51% | 30% | 29% | **−0.40** | 0.302 |
| 6-month  | 87 | **+5.65%** | +4.90% | +5.12% | 26% | 25% | **+0.36** | 0.679 |
| 12-month | 84 | **+11.39%** | +10.55% | +10.79% | 20% | 19% | **+0.27** | 0.635 |

Read it carefully, because the sign **isn't even stable**. At the short horizons (1–3
months) forward returns after falling quits are *marginally* below the base rate — the
folklore's direction, but at a trivial Welch *t* of **−0.40**. By 6–12 months it has
**flipped**: falling quits are followed by *higher*-than-average returns (**+11.4% vs
+10.8%** at 12 months, *t* = **+0.27**). Nothing clears even |*t*| = 0.5, the down-rate is
indistinguishable from base at every horizon, and the direction reverses with the horizon.
This is what *no* forward-return information looks like.

## The decisive test — does the quits downturn *lead* the market?

The pitch is that quits *lead* the cycle. So we scan the correlation of quits momentum at
*t* against the SPY return over `[t+L, t+L+1]`. A genuine leading gauge would show its
strongest *positive* correlation at a **positive** lead (quits move first — falling quits,
then a lower market later, i.e. rising quits then a higher market).

| lead *L* (months) | −4 | −3 | −1 | 0 | +1 | +3 | +6 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr(quits-mom, fwd SPY) | **+0.22** | +0.20 | −0.04 | +0.06 | +0.08 | +0.03 | −0.06 |

The strongest positive correlation sits at **L = −4** (with −3 close behind) — quits
momentum is most associated with the market move *three-to-four months in its **past***.
At the positive leads a real early-warning needs, the correlation is a flat **≈ +0.03 to
+0.08**. The quits rate isn't leading equities; it's a **coincident-to-lagging** echo of a
market that already turned — and then the ~6-week publication delay pushes even that echo
further out of reach. That is the core of the "leading gauge? — Not supported" stamp.

## Tradability — the "go to cash when quits are falling" overlay

Hold SPY when quits are rising, sit in cash when falling (two-month lag; 10 bps per
switch, turnover one-way × NAV). Sharpe is excess-of-zero (the cash leg earns 0 here — a
conservative, labelled simplification).

| book | ann. mean | ann. Sharpe | ann. vol | terminal $1 | switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-and-hold SPY | **+9.7%** | **0.64** | 15.1% | **8.7×** | — |
| overlay, gross | +8.1% | 0.69 | — | — | 90 |
| overlay, net @ 10 bps | **+7.8%** | **0.66** | 11.8% | **6.0×** | 90 |

The overlay's Sharpe (**0.66**) barely edges buy-and-hold's (**0.64**) — a rounding
difference — and it does so only by **being out of the market ~29% of the time**, so it
forfeits **~2 points of annual return** and lands at **6.0×** terminal wealth versus
**8.7×**. That is not alpha; it is **beta you de-risked**. Risk-matched, the tiny Sharpe
"win" evaporates — and you've paid for it with a third of your terminal wealth. Nothing
extractable, exactly the [Study 384](../384-ism-pmi-regime/) pattern (less exposure
masquerading as skill).

## The cyclicals leg — the "risk-appetite" tape goes the *wrong* way

The claim specifically names cyclicals. So we run the same split on a monthly-rebalanced
**XLY − XLP** (discretionary minus staples) long-short — the classic risk-appetite spread.

| horizon | n falling | falling mean | base mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 89 | +0.28% | +0.34% | −0.10 | 0.451 |
| 6-month  | 87 | **+3.15%** | +1.72% | +1.14 | 0.917 |
| 12-month | 84 | **+6.33%** | +3.64% | +1.66 | 0.969 |

If falling quits foretold cyclical weakness, the spread should be *negative* after a quits
downturn. Instead it is *more positive* than base at 6–12 months (**+6.3% vs +3.6%**,
*t* = +1.66 — the wrong sign for the claim, and still short of significance). Cyclicals
tend to *lead the recovery* the falling-quits reading is lagging into, so "sell cyclicals
when quits fall" is, if anything, backwards.

## Robustness — window, threshold, and the COVID dependence (12-month SPY)

| variation | n falling | falling 12m mean | base 12m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| momentum **k = 1** | 85 | +9.5% | +10.8% | −0.61 | 0.227 |
| momentum **k = 3** (base) | 84 | +11.4% | +10.8% | **+0.27** | 0.635 |
| momentum **k = 6** | 97 | +13.8% | +10.8% | **+1.33** | 0.971 |
| threshold **> 0.2 pp** | 19 | +12.4% | +10.8% | +0.26 | 0.660 |
| **drop 2020–2021** (ex-COVID) | 80 | +11.0% | +11.8% | −0.37 | 0.321 |

The sign is a coin-flip of the window: the slow (k = 6) filter turns *positive* (falling
quits → *higher* returns), the fast (k = 1) filter turns *negative*, and neither is close
to significant. No specification survives; the "signal" is noise you can point in either
direction by choosing a lookback.

## The publication-delay tax — lag sensitivity (12-month)

| execution lag | Welch *t* | note |
|---|--:|---|
| 0 months (look-ahead — not tradable) | −0.25 | you'd need the print the instant the month closed |
| 1 month | +0.10 | still faster than JOLTS actually reports |
| **2 months (honest JOLTS release lag)** | **+0.27** | the earliest you can really act |

Even the *look-ahead* version (act the instant the reference month ends, before JOLTS is
published) is insignificant and near zero — so there is no timing edge for the release lag
to erode. The delay just confirms there was never anything to be early with.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly quits + SPY-like series with a *planted* link (falling quits
momentum at *t* depresses the *t+1* return by `edge`). The detector + inference must
recover a planted edge and must **not** manufacture bearish significance when the true edge
is zero.

| planted edge (monthly) | n falling | falling 1m mean | base 1m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 138 | +1.48% | +1.03% | **+1.15** | 0.905 |
| **+0.04** (large link) | 138 | −1.92% | −0.85% | **−2.64** | 0.002 |

With **no** planted link the test shows no *bearish* false positive (*t* = +1.15, placebo
*p* = 0.91 — the opposite of significant-and-negative); a large planted link drives *t* to
**−2.64** (*p* = 0.002). The machinery is unbiased and powered — so the real-tape near-zero
*t* is a *genuine* absence of edge, not a broken test.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The quits rate carries no reliable forward-return information: the
  best Welch *t* across horizons is **−0.40**, the sign **flips** from (weakly) bearish at
  1–3 months to (weakly) bullish at 6–12 months, the down-rate matches base everywhere, and
  the effect can be pointed either way by the lookback window. The named cyclicals leg goes
  the **wrong** way. Indistinguishable from noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The cash-when-falling overlay's Sharpe (**0.66**) is a
  rounding-tie with buy-and-hold (**0.64**), bought only by sitting out ~29% of months —
  forfeiting **~2 pts/yr** and a third of terminal wealth (**6.0× vs 8.7×**). Beta you
  de-risked, not alpha you found; and every trade acts on a 6-week-old print.
- **Leading gauge? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The lead/lag scan peaks (positively) at **L = −4**
  months — quits momentum lags the market by a quarter — and is flat at the positive leads a
  real early-warning needs. A coincident-to-lagging echo, published ~6 weeks late. The whole
  appeal — a *leading* confidence gauge — is the part the data rejects.
